direction: D2: Case/experience memory instead of (or beside) rules: retrieve 2-3 similar past training cases into the solver prompt at solve time
refuted_claims:
R1. Claim: "its only robust gain is an answer leak" / "the only item fixed in both runs, '(Sir Francis) Drake', got it from case c28's own anchor reference". Checked v3_s1_train_rows.json, I-ds outputs for item 4b2b7d9b ("A knighted Englishman: The Golden Hind"). The v3 parent, with no cases, answered "Sir Francis Drake" in both runs and passed both. The fresh pilot parent answered "Francis Drake" twice. So the flip is drift in the fresh parent that the case arm happened to restore; against the historical parent it is a tie. No arm removed the anchor, and c28's lesson ("prefer the fullest standard form, including honorifics") plus the clue's "knighted" explain the answer just as well. So the leak is not shown to be the cause, and there is no robust gain of any kind. The leak RISK is still real: the case text does contain the answer. The 2 "ups" among the 73 v3 both-pass items are exactly this item and 07623a13. On 07623a13 v3 passed 2/2 using about 515 completion tokens, while the pilot parent hit the pilot's own 8,192 cap in both runs. One of the "3 leak items" (1bf040d1, "the leaves") is only a generic word match with c22's leaf-cutter-ant text.
R2. Claim: "short-answer QA gains are small (~+3)" (also in verdict_cn). Checked Memento (arXiv 2508.16153). On the DeepResearcher suite (seven open-domain short-answer QA sets) F1 goes 59.9->66.6 and PM 72.2->80.4. On SimpleQA F1 is +3.7 but PM is 89.7->95.0 (+5.3); the report quotes the smaller metric. LEAP's abstract gives DROP +7.5, a reading task with a given passage that is closer to SearchQA-with-snippets than HotpotQA. The literature range on QA is about +3 to +9, still against baselines without a task card.
R3. Claim: "cross-dataset transfer is carried by abstracted insights, i.e. rules, not by retrieved cases"; "a case bank is bench-local by construction" (verdict_cn says the same). Memento builds its case bank from NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA/2Wiki training trajectories. On out-of-distribution sets: MuSiQue 35.6->40.6, Bamboogle 77.5->86.2, PopQA 57.9->64.0 F1 (the paper's text says +4.7 to +9.6). The report's own literature table lists this result, which contradicts its implication #5. ExpeL's FEVER transfer (verified 63->70) used insights only because "we do not have an experience pool to retrieve from". Case transfer was never tried there, so ExpeL cannot show that cases fail to transfer. Locality is a design choice in D2, and cross-benchmark retrieval for the registered SearchQA<->OfficeQA pair was never piloted. Caveat: Memento's cases are planning trajectories of a search agent, so transfer to our fixed-snippet solver is uncertain.
R4. Claim: oracle "at most about +2 points on the panel"; "even the oracle bound is about +2 points", so no pilot limit could reveal a gain. Recomputed: 3 up / 1 down / 23 ties, +0.074. My bootstrap CI is [-0.019, +0.185] (theirs [-0.019, +0.204]), so the panel-level upper end is about +5 points, not +2. Two of the 3 oracle ups (fbed9ad1 "Marie-Antoinette" hyphen, 8f3603a1 paraphrase) are items mixed in v3 that also flipped in the lexical arm with unrelated cases, which points to noise. The oracle reuses the same 30 flawed cases, so it bounds nothing about a better bank. D9 measured that per-item oracle hints fixed 85% of 23 always-failed SearchQA items, and an "answer has N words" hint fixed 30%.
R5. Claim: ALFWorld study "~36M tokens with short guidelines, up to ~70M". I recomputed 105,651 tokens per I-ds episode over 31.3 calls on the new machine; correct. But AutoGuide identifies the context "at each timestep" (verified), and the 36M includes none of those calls. At about 3.4k tokens per call on the two memory arms they add about 24M (about 60M in total). With the report's own +2-8k tokens per call for full demonstrations, 228 memory-arm episodes x 31.3 calls give about 50-93M, not "up to ~70M".
R6. Claim: the case block "changed the final answer in 22 of 200 runs (15 items)". Recount: 20 of 198 runs (14 items) where both arms delivered an answer. The other 2 runs are parent truncations caused by the 8,192 cap.
R7. Claim: AWM "abstract beats concrete (45.1 vs 43.4)". That holds only for Mind2Web step SR; on WebArena rule-based scores 35.6 vs LM-based 35.5. The "7.9->5.9 steps" pairs the 15.0% ax-tree baseline, not the 23.5% one.
R8. Recommendations rest on mechanisms that D4 measured as ineffective: retrieval via "the D4 applicability judge with abstention" and recommendation 2(a). D4 found judged conditions at the base rate (median lift 1.02 against the target codes) and own-arm movement of 19.4% in scope vs 18.9% out of scope (p = 0.60). In D2's own pilot the solver ignored the header "use a case only if the same situation applies": c20's condition (the clue gives the first name) is absent from the Reagan and Alley questions. "Do NOT replace rules" is also asymmetric. The pilot had no rule arm, v3 accepted 0 of 49 rules, and D4 shows the v3 surname-only RULE I-ds s1-r1 also concentrated harm (2 up / 6 down in scope). The pilot therefore measures lesson content, not memory versus rules.
confirmed_claims:
Recomputed independently from data/pilot/cells.jsonl (checksums identical to /data/feasibility/D2):
- 400 cells, 2 parent truncations at 8,192, none tagless, rescoring 0 mismatches.
- cases vs fresh parent 5/7/88, mean -0.010, CI [-0.060, +0.040], p 0.77; accuracy 149/200 vs 147/200.
- Truncated runs excluded: 4/7/88, -0.015.
- Fresh vs v3 parent 3/7/90, -0.030; cases vs v3 parent 5/11/84, -0.040.
- By v3 pattern: both-pass 73 items 2 up / 5 down; mixed 9 items 2/1; both-fail 18 items 1/1.
- c20 retrieved for 23/100 items; harms on Reagan, Alley, Bush, Kahlo confirmed.
- 3 items have their reference inside a retrieved case; 0 overlap between case sources and evaluated items.
- Oracle 3/1/23, +0.074; item SD 0.245, giving 149/412/926 items for +5/+3/+2 points as single tests.
- +349 prompt tokens per cell (+9.3%); Skill 14,116-14,419 bytes.
- Tokens: 1,619,278 + 226,144 + 68,356 = 1,913,778.
- Bank of 30 cases with codes D1 11, D2 8, D5 5, D4 3, ...
Fidelity to v3: the solver prompt matches the frozen backends.solve for SearchQA and the scorer matches score() (evaluate em). evaluator.py, weak_solver_probe.py and validator_pilot/api.py are byte-identical between /data/skillopt-work and the v3 snapshot.
v3 facts: the stage code tables match stages.log; ALFWorld I-ds episodes average 105,651 tokens over 31.3 calls (recomputed); 21 shared normalised answers and OfficeQA 29/74 shared issues match the logs.
Literature checked against the papers:
- ExpeL: HotpotQA 28->39 (insights only 36, retrieval only 31); ALFWorld 40->59 (50/55); FEVER 63->70; the no-experience-pool sentence.
- AutoGuide: 54.5/59.0/79.1; WebShop 30/35/46 (Reflexion 51); Reddit 8.0/21.8/47.1; k 30/42/46/47/43; context-only 36 / guideline-only 37 / both 46; abstains when no context matches.
- Dynamic Cheatsheet: GPT-4o MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2->44.0/51.2; 4o-mini AIME 16.7->13.3.
- ACE: all numbers, quotes and helpful/harmful counters.
- ReasoningBank: 40.5/42.1/44.1/48.8; k 39.0/49.7/46.0/45.5/44.4; failures ablation.
- RICP: -0.2 to +4.3 (maths to +7.0). LEAP: +3.3 HotpotQA.
- Memento F1 numbers as quoted.
- Xiong et al.: ACL 2026 long.27, pp. 623-645; "flat or declining" quote.
The direction-level conclusion holds: no detectable gain over the task card on SearchQA, and the bank does not serve the co-evolution purpose.
missing:
1. No placebo or shuffled-memory arm. The -1 point cannot be separated from a generic added-text effect (cal-1 placebos moved -9.8 / +3.6 points).
2. The pilot tested a bank the project's own leakage layer would reject: every case states its source's reference answer. The lessons also contradict each other (c06 "drop titles" vs c03/c28 "include honorifics"), contain impossible steps (c10 "if wrong, retry with only the surname"), and state answer-distribution rules (c28 "most likely reference answer") that the writer prompt forbade. The recommended design (abstract anchors + judge) is untested.
3. Cross-benchmark retrieval, the owner's yardstick (e.g. a SearchQA bank retrieved on OfficeQA), was neither tested nor estimated.
4. No head-to-head comparison with rules.
5. The simplest case memory, KATE-style nearest-neighbour (question, gold answer) demonstrations, was not tried.
6. Test-time retrieval puts a GLM judge in the inference path. That changes what a "Skill" is, adds cost per test item, and breaks test-evaluation reuse; none of this is costed.
7. Recommendation 2(b): "paired" helpful/harmful tallies need rule-on/off counterfactual runs. Their cost and power are not given, and most cases are retrieved fewer than 15 times per 100 items.
8. The gate needs two lower bounds > 0 at once. At the stated n the joint power is about 0.67-0.71 (simulated); 80% needs about 190 items for +5 points instead of 149, and more if shuffled memory has a generic effect of its own.
9. The ALFWorld literature gains come from weak GPT-3.5 ReAct few-shot baselines, the same caveat the report applies to QA. D9 puts ALFWorld's text-fixable ceiling at +11 points, with 78% of the failure mass dead.
notes_cn: 核对结果：主要数字属实（5 题变好、7 题变差，平均低 1 分；提示词和评分与 v3 一致），"案例记忆在 SearchQA（检索问答）上没收益"成立，可行性仍低。需更正：①"唯一稳定变好的题是泄题"不成立，这题 v3 原说明书两遍都答对，是新一轮自己答错，没有稳定收益；②文献中案例记忆在短答案问答上可涨 5 到 9 分，也能迁移到相似数据集（Memento）；③"最多多对 2 题"只是 4 道题的估计，上限约 5 题；④ALFWorld（文字家务任务）实验漏算每步检索调用，约 6000 万而非 3600 万 token。试点缺随机案例对照；"只写姓"内容做成规则也有害，问题在内容不在形式。
